summary: API gateway 5xx cliff after scheduled batch-queue flush — upstream runtimes saturating
description:
Issue summary: BrightLearn reported a sudden elevation in 5xx responses (502/503) for API routes serving small prompt requests starting ~2026-03-10T15:12Z. Impact: several customers experienced failures in chat completions and short embedding calls; BrightLearn (dedicated tenant) saw 40% of requests failing for a 6-minute window. Environment: prod-us-east (dedicated cluster for BrightLearn), models: redwood-open-13B and redwood-opt-7B.

Observed behavior: Around 15:12 UTC the apigw error rate rockets from baseline 0.2% to 28% within 90s. Accept queue length climbs sharply on edge proxies; upstream serving runtime pool reports rapid worker creation, OOM-like logs, and frequent preempt/restart events. Simultaneously, the scheduler performed a configured batch-queue flush job (scheduled maintenance task) that triggered eviction of queued requests.

Steps to reproduce: 1) On prod with tenant BrightLearn, trigger a batch-queue flush for small-payload routes (test route: /v1/chat/complete?tenant=brightlearn). 2) Ramp a steady small-payload traffic at 300 rps (simulated client). 3) Observe apigw accept queue and runtime worker churn.

Logs & metrics (highlights): - apigw: 2026-03-10T15:12:31Z "upstream unavailable" spikes; 15:13:05Z many 502s with upstream reset. - runtime: repeated "worker init failed: EV_RETRY_LIMIT" and "pagefault: vm_prefault_failure" around same timestamps. - scheduler: scheduled job "batch-queue-flush" executed 15:11:58Z on cluster brightlearn-prod-01. - infra metrics: accept_queue_length from 12->780 in ~45s; runtime_active_workers doubled in 60s; kernel pagefaults and GC pause increased.

Hypothesis: The scheduled batch-queue flush created a synchronized eviction of long-tail queued requests causing a rapid flood of short-lived requests onto the serving runtime. The runtime's ephemeral worker pool attempted to scale up aggressively, oversubscribed local resources (CPU/memory) and caused worker init failures and pagefault spikes. The API gateway then observed unhealthy upstreams and returned 5xx errors. Additional factor: tenant-weight rebalancer had recently migrated a small fraction of traffic to this cluster which reduced headroom.

Immediate mitigation taken: - Disabled batch-queue-flush schedule for BrightLearn (15:20 UTC). - Applied temporary ingress rate-limit at apigw for tenant to 200 rps (15:22 UTC) while autoscaler tuning applied. - Drained a subset of prewarm ephemeral pools and restored a conservative prewarm size for small-payload routes (15:35 UTC). Result: apigw error rate returned to baseline by 15:38 UTC and customer confirmed normal traffic.

Root cause analysis (ongoing): We believe a combination of scheduled synchronous queue flush + reduced headroom after route-weight migration created a sudden demand spike that the runtime could not serve without fast-failure behavior. There may also be an uncovered bug where worker init races trigger repeated pagefaults under very high churn.

Next steps / action items: - SRE: confirm and instrument worker-init failure path; add tracing to worker bootstrap (owner: Diego). - Runtime team: reproduce worker init/pagefault pattern in staging with synthetic flush (owner: Priya Rao). - Scheduler: change batch-queue-flush to use jittered, tenant-scoped stagger (owner: Scheduler Team). - Console/Operations: Add runbook entry for "queue-flush-induced upstream saturation" and a guard to block flushes when accept_queue_length > 200 (owner: Ops). - Product: review recent tenant-weight migrations that affected BrightLearn (owner: Sarah Lee).

Customer communication: BrightLearn notified via support channel at 15:45 UTC with incident summary and interim mitigation. Follow-up scheduled: 2026-03-12 16:00 UTC postmortem call with customer and assigned engineers.
investigation_notes: 15:14 UTC: noticed apigw healthcheck probe failures correlate with worker init errors (SRE observation)
15:16 UTC: discovered scheduled batch-queue-flush executed at 15:11:58Z; backlog eviction produced burst of 700 reqs within 45s
15:25 UTC: runtime logs show repeated 'worker init failed: EV_RETRY_LIMIT' and 'vm_prefault_failure' on the same PID range
Heap/VM trace: spikes in pagefaults align with worker churn - possible memory pressure during rapid worker bootstrap
No NVML/GPU driver resets observed; issue appears CPU/memory/pagefault-bound rather than GPU reset
resolution_notes: Disabled scheduled flush and applied tenant ingress rate limit to stabilize traffic
Reduced prewarm for small-payload routes and implemented conservative autoscale ramp for ephemeral workers
Added a temporary scheduler guard to prevent global flushes during high accept_queue_length
Customer BrightLearn confirmed service recovery and accepted scheduled postmortem
